name: Sam Yagan
milestone_by_age_26: Co-founded SparkNotes, an online study guide company, during his senior year at Harvard in 1999 at age 22, and sold it for $30 million in 2000; later co-founded eDonkey (2002) and OkCupid (2003), all before age 26.
starting_point: Born in 1977 to Syrian immigrant parents in Chicago; attended Illinois Mathematics and Science Academy before Harvard.
current_position: Co-founder and managing director of Corazon Capital, a Chicago-based early-stage venture capital firm; formerly CEO of ShopRunner (sold to FedEx in 2020) and CEO of Match Group.

trajectory.title: Co-founded SparkNotes at Harvard
trajectory.description: During his senior year at Harvard, Yagan co-founded TheSpark.com (later SparkNotes) with classmates Chris Coyne, Max Krohn, and Christian Rudder.

trajectory.title: Sold SparkNotes for $30 million
trajectory.description: Sold SparkNotes to iTurf Inc. for $30 million, becoming a dot-com-era millionaire; the deal closed weeks before the dot-com bubble burst.

trajectory.title: Oversaw SparkNotes transition to Barnes & Noble
trajectory.description: Stayed at Barnes & Noble as VP and Publisher after SparkNotes was re-sold, expanding the digital brand into a multi-platform media business.

trajectory.title: Co-founded eDonkey
trajectory.description: Co-founded eDonkey, a peer-to-peer file-sharing network that became one of the largest P2P platforms in the world.

trajectory.title: Co-founded OkCupid
trajectory.description: Teamed up again with his Harvard classmates to found OkCupid, an online dating site built on a question-and-answer matching system.

trajectory.title: Co-founded Excelerate Labs (TechStars Chicago)
trajectory.description: Co-founded the startup accelerator Excelerate Labs, which later became TechStars Chicago, grooming early-stage entrepreneurs.

trajectory.title: Sold OkCupid to Match Group for $50M
trajectory.description: Led the sale of OkCupid to Match Group (IAC subsidiary) and became CEO of Match Group.

trajectory.title: Co-founded Corazon Capital
trajectory.description: Co-founded Corazon Capital with Steve Farsht, focusing on early-stage consumer internet investments.

trajectory.title: Led Match Group IPO
trajectory.description: As CEO, led Match Group through its IPO; transitioned to Vice-Chairman of the board at the end of 2015.

trajectory.title: Became CEO of ShopRunner
trajectory.description: Joined ShopRunner as CEO, a membership-based free two-day shipping service; led the company's sale to FedEx in 2020.

name: Jawed Karim
milestone_by_age_26: Co-founded YouTube in February 2005 at age 25, the world's largest video-sharing platform, which was acquired by Google in 2006 for $1.65 billion.
starting_point: Born in 1979 in Merseburg, East Germany, to a Bangladeshi researcher father and German biochemist mother; family fled racism, immigrating to Saint Paul, Minnesota in 1992.
current_position: Co-founder of YouTube and venture investor; maintains a low public profile; net worth estimated in the hundreds of millions from Google shares and early Airbnb investment.

trajectory.title: Graduated high school in Minnesota
trajectory.description: Graduated from Saint Paul Central High School and enrolled at the University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign for computer science.

trajectory.title: Joined PayPal as early engineer
trajectory.description: Left university early to join PayPal, where he designed core components including the real-time anti-fraud system and met future YouTube co-founders.

trajectory.title: Completed BS at University of Illinois
trajectory.description: Completed his Bachelor of Science in computer science while working at PayPal.

trajectory.title: Co-founded YouTube and uploaded first video
trajectory.description: Co-founded YouTube with Chad Hurley and Steve Chen in February 2005; uploaded the first video 'Me at the zoo' on April 23, 2005.

trajectory.title: YouTube acquired by Google for $1.65B
trajectory.description: YouTube was acquired by Google for $1.65 billion in stock; Karim received 137,443 shares of Google stock.

trajectory.title: Co-founded Y Ventures (Youniversity Ventures)
trajectory.description: Launched a venture fund with Kevin Hartz and Keith Rabois; made an early $30K investment in Airbnb that grew to be worth tens of millions.

trajectory.title: Enrolled at Stanford for graduate studies
trajectory.description: Enrolled as a graduate student in computer science at Stanford University while serving as an informal advisor to YouTube.

name: Andrew McCollum
milestone_by_age_26: Co-founded Facebook in February 2004 at age 20, one of the most consequential social media companies in history, alongside Mark Zuckerberg, Dustin Moskovitz, and Chris Hughes.
starting_point: Born in 1983 in California; attended Harvard University where he met Mark Zuckerberg through computer science classes.
current_position: CEO of Philo, an internet television streaming company; based in San Francisco.

trajectory.title: Co-founded Facebook at Harvard
trajectory.description: Joined Mark Zuckerberg, Dustin Moskovitz, and Chris Hughes to launch TheFacebook.com in February 2004, handling graphics and design.

trajectory.title: Worked on Wirehog
trajectory.description: Developed Wirehog, a file-sharing program, alongside Adam D'Angelo; left Harvard to work full-time at Facebook in Palo Alto.

trajectory.title: Returned to Harvard
trajectory.description: Returned to Harvard College to complete his bachelor's degree in computer science after working at Facebook for over a year.

trajectory.title: Graduated from Harvard
trajectory.description: Graduated from Harvard with a degree in computer science; later earned a master's in education from Harvard Graduate School of Education.

trajectory.title: Co-founded JobSpice
trajectory.description: Co-founded JobSpice, an online resume preparation tool, after leaving Facebook.

trajectory.title: Became Entrepreneur in Residence
trajectory.description: Served as Entrepreneur in Residence at Flybridge Capital Partners and New Enterprise Associates.

trajectory.title: Became CEO of Philo
trajectory.description: Named CEO of Philo (then Philo Internet Television), succeeding Christopher Thorpe; led the live TV streaming service.

name: Steve Chen
milestone_by_age_26: Co-founded YouTube in February 2005 at age 26, the world's largest video-sharing platform, and served as its CTO. YouTube was acquired by Google in 2006 for $1.65 billion.
starting_point: Born in 1978 in Taipei, Taiwan; immigrated to the US at age 8, settling in Illinois; attended Illinois Mathematics and Science Academy and University of Illinois.
current_position: Entrepreneur in residence at Google Ventures; based in Taipei, Taiwan; received the first Taiwan Employment Gold Card.

trajectory.title: Left university for Silicon Valley
trajectory.description: Left the University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign to join PayPal in Silicon Valley, where he met Chad Hurley and Jawed Karim.

trajectory.title: Co-founded YouTube as CTO
trajectory.description: Co-founded YouTube with Hurley and Karim in February 2005; served as Chief Technology Officer overseeing product engineering and design.

trajectory.title: YouTube acquired by Google for $1.65B
trajectory.description: Sold YouTube to Google for $1.65 billion in stock; received 625,366 shares of Google plus additional shares in a trust.

trajectory.title: Co-founded AVOS Systems
trajectory.description: Co-founded AVOS Systems with Chad Hurley; acquired Delicious from Yahoo and built MixBit, a video-sharing platform.

trajectory.title: Joined Google Ventures
trajectory.description: Joined Google Ventures (now GV) as Entrepreneur in Residence.

trajectory.title: Co-founded Nom.com
trajectory.description: Started a live-streaming food network with Vijay Karunamurthy; the venture shut down in 2017.

trajectory.title: Moved to Taipei
trajectory.description: Relocated to Taipei, Taiwan, receiving the first Taiwan Employment Gold Card and working to enhance Taiwan's startup community.

name: Jeremy Stoppelman
milestone_by_age_26: Co-founded Yelp in summer 2004 at age 26, building it into a major local-search and review platform that went public in 2012 with a market capitalization of approximately $4 billion.
starting_point: Born in 1977 in Arlington, Virginia; mother was an English teacher, father a securities lawyer; began investing in stocks at age 14.
current_position: Co-founder and CEO of Yelp Inc.; net worth estimated at several hundred million dollars.

trajectory.title: Graduated from University of Illinois
trajectory.description: Obtained a bachelor's degree in computer engineering from the University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign.

trajectory.title: Joined PayPal as engineer
trajectory.description: Joined X.com (later PayPal) as a software engineer; rose to VP of Engineering, becoming part of the PayPal Mafia.

trajectory.title: Left PayPal for Harvard Business School
trajectory.description: Left PayPal after its eBay acquisition and enrolled at Harvard Business School for one year.

trajectory.title: Co-founded Yelp
trajectory.description: During a summer internship at MRL Ventures, co-founded Yelp with Russel Simmons, developing the local review platform.

trajectory.title: Rejected Google acquisition offer
trajectory.description: Turned down a reported $500 million acquisition offer from Google, choosing to keep Yelp independent.

trajectory.title: Led Yelp IPO
trajectory.description: Took Yelp public on the NYSE; the IPO valued the company at approximately $4 billion.

trajectory.title: Yelp reached $1B+ revenue
trajectory.description: Continued leading Yelp as CEO, growing the platform to serve millions of users and businesses across 39 countries.

name: Chris Hughes
milestone_by_age_26: Co-founded Facebook in 2004 at age 20, serving as spokesman and early product/UX contributor during its initial growth from Harvard to a multi-school platform.
starting_point: Born in 1983 in Hickory, North Carolina; only child of an industrial paper salesman and a mathematics teacher; raised as an evangelical Lutheran; attended Phillips Academy Andover.
current_position: Chair of the Economic Security Project; author of 'Marketcrafters' (2025); completing PhD at Wharton; lives in New York's Greenwich Village.

trajectory.title: Co-founded Facebook at Harvard
trajectory.description: Joined Zuckerberg's founding team as spokesman and product contributor, focusing on user experience and site functionality.

trajectory.title: Graduated Harvard and rejoined Facebook
trajectory.description: Graduated from Harvard with a BA in History and Literature, magna cum laude; relocated to Palo Alto to rejoin Facebook.

trajectory.title: Left Facebook
trajectory.description: Departed Facebook with a small stake in the company; later earned approximately $500 million from the 2012 IPO.

trajectory.title: Directed online organizing for Obama campaign
trajectory.description: Joined Barack Obama's presidential campaign as Director of Online Organizing, spearheading my.barackobama.com.

trajectory.title: Founded Jumo
trajectory.description: Named Entrepreneur in Residence at General Catalyst; founded Jumo, a social network for nonprofit organizations.

trajectory.title: Bought The New Republic
trajectory.description: Became publisher and editor-in-chief of The New Republic, a century-old political magazine.

trajectory.title: Co-founded Economic Security Project
trajectory.description: Co-founded the Economic Security Project, advocating for universal basic income and economic reform.

trajectory.title: Called for Facebook breakup
trajectory.description: Published a New York Times op-ed calling for Facebook to be broken up and for increased tech regulation.

name: Janus Friis
milestone_by_age_26: Co-founded KaZaA in 2000-2001 at age 24, which became the world's most popular peer-to-peer file-sharing application after Napster's shutdown, with hundreds of millions of downloads globally by age 25-26.
starting_point: Born in 1976 in Copenhagen, Denmark; dropped out of high school; taught himself computer skills while working at a help desk at CyberCity, one of Denmark's first ISPs.
current_position: Danish entrepreneur; maintains a relatively low profile; formerly co-founder of Skype, KaZaA, Joost, and Rdio.

trajectory.title: Met Niklas Zennström at Tele2
trajectory.description: While working in customer support at Tele2's Danish branch, met his future business partner Niklas Zennström.

trajectory.title: Co-founded KaZaA in Amsterdam
trajectory.description: Moved into Zennström's apartment in Amsterdam to develop KaZaA, building the FastTrack P2P protocol that became the world's most popular file-sharing software.

trajectory.title: Co-founded Skype
trajectory.description: Co-founded Skype, the peer-to-peer telephony application that made free international voice calls a reality for hundreds of millions.

trajectory.title: Sold Skype to eBay for $2.6B
trajectory.description: Sold Skype to eBay for US$2.6 billion; maintained ownership interest through Silver Lake Partners.

trajectory.title: Co-founded Joost
trajectory.description: Co-founded Joost, an internet TV service using P2P technology; the venture struggled and was eventually shut down.

trajectory.title: Co-founded Rdio
trajectory.description: Co-founded the online music streaming service Rdio with Zennström; it filed for bankruptcy in 2015 and assets were sold to Pandora for $75 million.

name: John Romero
milestone_by_age_26: Co-founded id Software on February 1, 1991 at age 23, shipped the seminal Commander Keen series (December 1990), Wolfenstein 3D (May 1992), and Doom (December 1993) by age 26, games that defined and popularized the first-person shooter genre.
starting_point: Born in 1967 in Colorado Springs, Colorado; self-taught programmer who started making games on an Apple II at age 13; of Mexican, Yaqui, and Cherokee heritage.
current_position: Co-founder of Romero Games Ltd. based in Galway, Ireland; continues developing games; received Emmy awards for 3D software engine technology.

trajectory.title: Published first game in magazine
trajectory.description: Published his first game 'Scout Search' as a type-in program in Apple II magazine inCider; published over 12 games under Capitol Ideas Software.

trajectory.title: Joined Softdisk
trajectory.description: Joined Softdisk Publishing in Shreveport, Louisiana, where he met John Carmack, Tom Hall, and Adrian Carmack.

trajectory.title: Co-founded id Software
trajectory.description: Co-founded id Software on February 1, 1991, departing Softdisk with Carmack, Hall, and Carmack to form the legendary game studio.

trajectory.title: Released Wolfenstein 3D
trajectory.description: Designed Wolfenstein 3D (May 1992), which popularized the first-person shooter genre and coined the term 'deathmatch'.

trajectory.title: Released Doom
trajectory.description: Designed and shipped Doom (December 1993), one of the most influential video games ever, defining the FPS genre.

trajectory.title: Left id Software
trajectory.description: Was forced out of id Software due to disputes with Carmack over work intensity and the development of Quake.

trajectory.title: Co-founded Ion Storm
trajectory.description: Co-founded Ion Storm in Dallas; directed Daikatana (2000), which was a critical and commercial failure.

trajectory.title: Released SIGIL
trajectory.description: Released SIGIL, an officially licensed fifth episode for Doom, demonstrating his enduring connection to the franchise.

trajectory.title: Founded Romero Games
trajectory.description: Founded Romero Games Ltd. in Galway, Ireland, with his wife Brenda Romero, continuing his game development career.

name: Teresa Teng
milestone_by_age_26: Began her professional singing career in 1967 (age 14) with her first album release, TV hosting role, and record contract. By 1968 (age 15), she achieved widespread fame in Taiwan through 'The Gathering of Stars' TV program. By age 26 (1979), she was a dominant pop star across Asia with multiple hit albums, concerts in Southeast Asia, and recordings in multiple languages.
starting_point: Born in 1953 in Baozhong, Yunlin, Taiwan, to a mainlander military family; father was a Nationalist military officer who fled mainland China.
current_position: Died on May 8, 1995 at age 42 in Chiang Mai, Thailand, from a severe asthma attack; was one of the most influential Asian musicians of all time.

trajectory.title: Won children's singing competition
trajectory.description: Won a local singing competition in Taiwan, demonstrating her precocious vocal talent.

trajectory.title: Began professional singing career
trajectory.description: Released her first album and secured a TV hosting role, launching her professional music career.

trajectory.title: Achieved widespread fame in Taiwan
trajectory.description: Gained national fame through 'The Gathering of Stars' TV program, becoming a household name in Taiwan.

trajectory.title: Breakthrough in Japan
trajectory.description: Entered the Japanese music market, becoming a successful singer of Japanese ballads and expanding her pan-Asian fame.

trajectory.title: Dominant pop star across Asia
trajectory.description: Established as a dominant pop star across East and Southeast Asia with hit albums and concerts in multiple languages.

trajectory.title: Peak of career with 15th Anniversary Tour
trajectory.description: Reached career zenith with a mammoth Fifteenth Anniversary Tour including six consecutive sold-out days at the Hong Kong Coliseum.

trajectory.title: Supported democracy at Hong Kong concert
trajectory.description: Performed at a Hong Kong rally wearing a 'Democracy Lives' headband eight days before the Tiananmen Square crackdown.

trajectory.title: Died in Chiang Mai, Thailand
trajectory.description: Died from a severe asthma attack on May 8, 1995, while visiting Thailand; mourned across the Chinese-speaking world.

name: Gianna Nannini
milestone_by_age_26: Released her self-titled debut album in 1976 (age 22) and her second album 'Una Radura' in 1977. Her first domestic hit single 'America' and the album 'California' came in 1979 (age 25), making her a recognized figure in the Italian rock scene by age 26.
starting_point: Born in 1954 in Siena, Italy; daughter of a confectionery industrialist and Siena Football Club president; studied piano and composition in Milan; lost two phalanges of her left hand in a machine accident at the family pastry shop.
current_position: Active Italian rock singer and songwriter; continues touring and releasing music; turned 70 in 2024.

trajectory.title: First recording as vocalist
trajectory.description: Co-wrote and recorded the B-side 'Stereotipati Noi' for Flora Fauna e Cemento's single, her first professional recording.

trajectory.title: Released self-titled debut album
trajectory.description: Released her debut album 'Gianna Nannini' on Ricordi, establishing herself as a powerful female songwriter in the Italian rock scene.

trajectory.title: Released second album 'Una Radura'
trajectory.description: Released her sophomore album 'Una Radura,' continuing to develop her piano-based rock style.

trajectory.title: First domestic hit with 'America'
trajectory.description: Scored her first domestic hit single 'America' and released the album 'California,' becoming a recognized figure across Europe.

trajectory.title: International breakthrough with 'Puzzle'
trajectory.description: Released the Conny Plank-produced album 'Puzzle,' which peaked in the top 10 across Italian, German, Austrian, and Swiss charts.

trajectory.title: European hit 'Bello e impossibile'
trajectory.description: Released 'Bello e impossibile,' a major European hit across Italy, Germany, Austria, and Switzerland.

trajectory.title: Released greatest hits 'Perle'
trajectory.description: Released the greatest hits album 'Perle,' rearranging her most renowned songs with piano and string quartet.

trajectory.title: Released 'Amore Gigante'
trajectory.description: Released the album 'Amore Gigante' and toured extensively across Europe, continuing a career spanning over four decades.

name: Davor Šuker
milestone_by_age_26: Won the 1987 FIFA U-20 World Cup with Yugoslavia at age 19 (scoring 6 goals in 6 matches), and by 25-26 was among the top scorers in La Liga with 24 goals in the 1993-94 season for Sevilla.
starting_point: Born in 1968 in Osijek, Croatia (then Yugoslavia); began his footballing career at hometown club NK Osijek at age 16.
current_position: Former president of the Croatian Football Federation (2012-2021); retired from professional football in 2003; Croatia's all-time top scorer with 45 goals.

trajectory.title: Debuted for NK Osijek
trajectory.description: Made his senior debut for hometown club NK Osijek in the Yugoslav first division at age 16.

trajectory.title: Won FIFA U-20 World Cup
trajectory.description: Won the 1987 FIFA U-20 World Cup with Yugoslavia, scoring 6 goals in 6 matches as the tournament's standout striker.

trajectory.title: Transferred to Dinamo Zagreb
trajectory.description: Moved to Dinamo Zagreb, but the Croatian War of Independence cut short his promising season.

trajectory.title: Signed with Sevilla FC
trajectory.description: Transferred to Sevilla in La Liga, where he became one of the division's most consistent top scorers over five seasons.

trajectory.title: Signed with Real Madrid
trajectory.description: Joined Real Madrid for a significant fee; scored 24 goals in his first La Liga season and won the league title.

trajectory.title: World Cup Golden Boot and Champions League
trajectory.description: Won the Golden Boot at the 1998 World Cup with 6 goals, leading Croatia to third place; also won the UEFA Champions League with Real Madrid.

trajectory.title: Moved to Arsenal
trajectory.description: Transferred to Arsenal in the Premier League, later playing for West Ham United and 1860 Munich.

trajectory.title: Retired from professional football
trajectory.description: Retired from club football after a spell at 1860 Munich, ending a career with 203 goals in 448 club appearances.

trajectory.title: Elected president of Croatian Football Federation
trajectory.description: Became president of the Croatian Football Federation, serving until 2021.

name: Allan Simonsen
milestone_by_age_26: Won the 1977 Ballon d'Or (European Footballer of the Year) at age 24, the only Danish player ever to receive the award; earlier won the 1971 and 1972 Danish championships with Vejle BK and scored 3 goals at the 1972 Summer Olympics before transferring to Borussia Mönchengladbach.
starting_point: Born in 1952 in Vejle, Denmark; joined the youth team of local club Vejle BK at age 11; made his senior debut at 18.
current_position: Retired Danish footballer and manager; the only Danish player to win the Ballon d'Or; inducted into the Danish Football Hall of Fame in 2008.

trajectory.title: Senior debut and Danish championship with Vejle BK
trajectory.description: Made his senior debut for Vejle BK and won the 1971 Danish championship, immediately impressing with pace and finishing.

trajectory.title: Danish double and Olympics
trajectory.description: Won the 1972 Danish championship and cup double; scored 3 goals in 6 matches at the Munich Olympics, attracting European scouts.

trajectory.title: Transferred to Borussia Mönchengladbach
trajectory.description: Moved to Borussia Mönchengladbach in the Bundesliga for 200,000 Deutsche Mark after impressing coach Hennes Weisweiler at the Olympics.

trajectory.title: Bundesliga champion and UEFA Cup winner
trajectory.description: Broke into the starting lineup, scoring 18 goals as Mönchengladbach won the Bundesliga; scored 10 goals in 12 UEFA Cup games including two in the final.

trajectory.title: Won Ballon d'Or
trajectory.description: Named European Footballer of the Year (Ballon d'Or), the only Danish player ever to receive the award.

trajectory.title: Won UEFA Cup with Mönchengladbach
trajectory.description: Won his second UEFA Cup with Borussia Mönchengladbach, cementing his legacy at the club.

trajectory.title: Transferred to Barcelona
trajectory.description: Moved to Barcelona, where he won the 1982 Cup Winners' Cup and became a cult hero known as 'Simonet.'

trajectory.title: Moved to Charlton Athletic
trajectory.description: Left Barcelona for Charlton Athletic after Diego Maradona's arrival, later finishing his career in Denmark.

name: Hernán Crespo
milestone_by_age_26: Made his professional debut with River Plate in November 1993 at age 18, scoring 13 goals in 25 league appearances and winning the 1993 Apertura title; later won the 1996 Copa Libertadores at age 21, scoring twice in the final against América de Cali.
starting_point: Born in 1975 in Florida, Buenos Aires, Argentina; joined River Plate's youth academy at age 13.
current_position: Football manager; most recently coached Al-Duhail SC in Qatar; formerly managed São Paulo, Defensa y Justicia, and Banfield.

trajectory.title: Professional debut with River Plate
trajectory.description: Made his debut in the 1993-94 season, scoring 13 goals in 25 appearances and winning the Apertura title.

trajectory.title: Won Copa Libertadores with River Plate
trajectory.description: Scored twice in the Copa Libertadores final against América de Cali, securing River Plate's first continental title; also won Olympic silver.

trajectory.title: Transferred to Parma
trajectory.description: Moved to Parma in Serie A, where he won the 1999 UEFA Cup and Italian Cup.

trajectory.title: World record transfer to Lazio
trajectory.description: Became the world's most expensive player when Lazio paid £35 million; finished as Serie A top scorer with 26 goals in his first season.

trajectory.title: Joined Chelsea
trajectory.description: Transferred to Chelsea for £16.8 million; spent the 2004-05 season on loan at AC Milan, reaching the Champions League final.

trajectory.title: Joined Inter Milan
trajectory.description: Returned to Inter Milan, winning multiple Serie A titles as part of a dominant Inter squad.

trajectory.title: Retired as a player
trajectory.description: Retired from professional football after a final spell at Parma, having scored over 300 goals in a 19-year career.

trajectory.title: Began managerial career
trajectory.description: Transitioned to management, coaching clubs including Banfield, Defensa y Justicia, and São Paulo.

name: Agnetha Fältskog
milestone_by_age_26: Her self-penned debut single 'Jag var så kär' ('I Was So in Love') topped the Swedish sales chart on 28 January 1968 at age 17, selling over 80,000 copies and reaching #3 on Svensktoppen; her self-titled debut album followed in spring 1968, establishing her as one of Sweden's most popular pop artists.
starting_point: Born in 1950 in Jönköping, Sweden; daughter of a department store manager; wrote her first song at age six; started singing in a dance band at 16.
current_position: Retired from public life; resides on the Stockholm County island of Ekerö; reunited with ABBA for the Voyage album (2021) and concert residency.

trajectory.title: Recorded debut single 'Jag var så kär'
trajectory.description: Recorded her self-penned debut single on October 16, 1967; released through Cupol Records the following month.

trajectory.title: Debut single topped Swedish charts
trajectory.description: 'Jag var så kär' topped the Swedish sales chart on January 28, 1968, selling over 80,000 copies; debut album 'Agnetha' followed in spring.

trajectory.title: Met Björn Ulvaeus
trajectory.description: Met Björn Ulvaeus during a TV tribute show; the two began a romantic relationship that led to marriage in 1971.

trajectory.title: Joined ABBA formation
trajectory.description: Began performing with Björn Ulvaeus, Benny Andersson, and Anni-Frid Lyngstad; ABBA was formally constituted.

trajectory.title: ABBA won Eurovision
trajectory.description: ABBA won the Eurovision Song Contest with 'Waterloo,' launching international superstardom.

trajectory.title: ABBA unofficially disbanded
trajectory.description: ABBA went on indefinite hiatus; Agnetha pursued a solo career and acted in the Swedish film 'Raskenstam.'

trajectory.title: First English-language solo album
trajectory.description: Released 'Wrap Your Arms Around Me,' produced by Mike Chapman, launching her international solo career.

trajectory.title: Returned with 'My Colouring Book'
trajectory.description: Released her first album in 16 years, 'My Colouring Book,' ending a long period of reclusiveness.

trajectory.title: ABBA reunited for 'Voyage'
trajectory.description: Reunited with ABBA to release their ninth studio album 'Voyage' and launched the ABBA Voyage concert residency in London.

name: Sid Vicious
milestone_by_age_26: Was the bassist for the Sex Pistols during the release of 'Never Mind the Bollocks, Here's the Sex Pistols' (October 1977), one of the most influential punk rock albums ever recorded.
starting_point: Born Simon John Ritchie in 1957 in Lewisham, London; raised by a single mother who was a frequent drug user; grew up in poverty.
current_position: Died on February 2, 1979 at age 21 in New York City from a heroin overdose, while out on bail for the stabbing death of Nancy Spungen.

trajectory.title: Began music career in London punk scene
trajectory.description: Began his musical career as a fixture of the London punk scene, briefly involved with Siouxsie and the Banshees and The Flowers of Romance.

trajectory.title: Joined Sex Pistols as bassist
trajectory.description: Replaced Glen Matlock as bassist of the Sex Pistols in February 1977, despite having minimal ability to play the instrument.

trajectory.title: Released 'Never Mind the Bollocks'
trajectory.description: The Sex Pistols released their only studio album 'Never Mind the Bollocks, Here's the Sex Pistols' in October 1977, one of the most influential punk albums ever.

trajectory.title: Sex Pistols broke up
trajectory.description: The Sex Pistols disbanded after their final concert at the Winterland Ballroom in San Francisco on January 14, 1978.

trajectory.title: Nancy Spungen found dead
trajectory.description: Girlfriend Nancy Spungen was found stabbed to death on October 12, 1978, in their room at the Chelsea Hotel; Vicious was arrested for her murder.

trajectory.title: Died of heroin overdose
trajectory.description: Died on February 2, 1979, from a heroin overdose at a party celebrating his release on bail, just hours after being freed from Riker's Island.

name: Tony Adams
milestone_by_age_26: Won the Football League Cup with Arsenal in 1987 at age 20 and became Arsenal's youngest-ever captain at age 21 in January 1988, establishing himself as a first-team regular and England international by his early twenties.
starting_point: Born in 1966 in Romford, Greater London; grew up in Dagenham; signed for Arsenal as a schoolboy in 1980 at age 14.
current_position: Former footballer and manager; runs Sporting Chance Clinic; involved in football advisory roles; known as 'Mr. Arsenal.'

trajectory.title: Arsenal first-team debut
trajectory.description: Made his first-team debut for Arsenal on November 5, 1983, against Sunderland, aged 17.

trajectory.title: Won Football League Cup
trajectory.description: Won the Littlewoods Cup with Arsenal, beating Liverpool 2-1 in the final at Wembley.

trajectory.title: Became Arsenal's youngest-ever captain
trajectory.description: Appointed Arsenal captain in January 1988 at age 21, a position he held for 14 years until retirement.

trajectory.title: Led Arsenal to first league title in 18 years
trajectory.description: Captained Arsenal to their first league championship since 1971 in dramatic fashion at Anfield.

trajectory.title: Jailed for drink-driving

trajectory.title: Released 'The Number of the Beast'

trajectory.title: Released 'Piece of Mind'

trajectory.title: Released 'The Book of Souls'

name: Steve Ballmer
milestone_by_age_26: Joined Microsoft in June 1980 at age 24 as its 30th employee and first business manager, receiving $50,000 salary and 7% equity; by late 1981 (age 25) he helped secure the landmark IBM deal to outfit all new PCs with MS-DOS, one of the most consequential deals in tech history.
starting_point: Born in 1956 in Detroit, Michigan; son of a Swiss immigrant father who worked as a manager at Ford Motor Company; attended Harvard University, living down the hall from Bill Gates.
current_position: Owner of the LA Clippers; co-founder of Ballmer Group philanthropic fund; net worth estimated at over $150 billion as of 2024.

trajectory.title: Graduated from Harvard
trajectory.description: Graduated from Harvard with a BA in applied mathematics and economics; worked at Procter & Gamble.

trajectory.title: Joined Microsoft as 30th employee
trajectory.description: Hired by Bill Gates as Microsoft's first business manager; left Stanford MBA program to join.

trajectory.title: Secured landmark IBM deal
trajectory.description: Helped secure the IBM deal to outfit all new PCs with MS-DOS, one of the most consequential deals in tech history.

trajectory.title: Microsoft IPO
trajectory.description: Microsoft went public in March 1986, making Ballmer a multimillionaire through his equity stake.

trajectory.title: Promoted to President of Microsoft
trajectory.description: Promoted to President in July 1998, gaining day-to-day responsibility for running the company.

trajectory.title: Became CEO of Microsoft
trajectory.description: Succeeded Bill Gates as CEO of Microsoft on January 13, 2000.

trajectory.title: Retired as Microsoft CEO and bought Clippers
trajectory.description: Retired as CEO in February 2014; purchased the LA Clippers for $2 billion.

trajectory.title: Opened Intuit Dome
trajectory.description: Opened the $2 billion Intuit Dome as the new home of the LA Clippers; net worth exceeded $157 billion.

name: Andy Cole
milestone_by_age_26: In the 1993-94 season at age 22-23, Cole was the Premier League top scorer with 34 league goals (41 in all competitions) for Newcastle United, won the PFA Young Player of the Year award, and set a club record for goals in a season that still stands.
starting_point: Born in 1971 in Nottingham, England; began his youth career at Arsenal in 1988, signing professional in 1989.
current_position: Retired English footballer; works as a football coach and pundit; won 5 Premier League titles and the 1999 Treble with Manchester United.

trajectory.title: Signed professional with Arsenal
trajectory.description: Signed professional terms with Arsenal; made his league debut as a substitute in December 1990.

trajectory.title: Joined Bristol City
trajectory.description: After loans at Fulham and Bristol City, signed permanently with Bristol City, scoring prolifically.

trajectory.title: Signed with Newcastle United
trajectory.description: Transferred to Newcastle United, where he would have his breakout season.

trajectory.title: Premier League top scorer
trajectory.description: Scored 34 league goals (41 in all competitions) for Newcastle, winning the PFA Young Player of the Year award.

trajectory.title: Won Premier League with Manchester United
trajectory.description: Won his first Premier League title with Manchester United, scoring 11 league goals.

trajectory.title: Won the Treble with Manchester United
trajectory.description: Won the Premier League, FA Cup, and UEFA Champions League with Manchester United, forming a legendary partnership with Dwight Yorke.

trajectory.title: Left Manchester United
trajectory.description: Left Manchester United after scoring 121 goals in 275 appearances, joining Blackburn Rovers.

trajectory.title: Retired from professional football
trajectory.description: Retired after spells at multiple clubs including Blackburn, Fulham, Manchester City, and Sunderland.

name: Glenn Hughes
milestone_by_age_26: By age 22 (1973), Hughes joined Deep Purple — then one of the world's biggest rock bands — as bassist and co-lead vocalist, and by age 26 (1977) he had recorded three albums with them including the classic 'Burn' (1974), 'Stormbringer' (1974), and 'Come Taste the Band' (1975).
starting_point: Born in 1951 in Cannock, Staffordshire, England; fronted the band Finders Keepers in the 1960s as bassist and vocalist.
current_position: Active solo musician; fronts the supergroup Black Country Communion; inducted into Rock and Roll Hall of Fame as Deep Purple member in 2016.

trajectory.title: Released first album with Trapeze

trajectory.title: Joined Deep Purple
trajectory.description: Recruited to replace Roger Glover as bassist in Deep Purple, sharing lead vocal duties with David Coverdale.

trajectory.title: Released 'Burn' with Deep Purple
trajectory.description: Recorded the classic Deep Purple album 'Burn,' one of the band's most acclaimed records.

trajectory.title: Released 'Stormbringer'
trajectory.description: Recorded 'Stormbringer' with Deep Purple, continuing the Mk. III lineup's output.

trajectory.title: Deep Purple disbanded
trajectory.description: Deep Purple broke up in 1976 after the 'Come Taste the Band' album; Hughes embarked on a solo career battling addiction.

trajectory.title: Released first solo album 'Play Me Out'
trajectory.description: Released his debut solo album while battling severe cocaine addiction.

trajectory.title: Briefly fronted Black Sabbath
trajectory.description: Fronted Black Sabbath in the mid-1980s, recording the album 'Seventh Star' (originally a Tony Iommi solo project).

trajectory.title: Inducted into Rock and Roll Hall of Fame
trajectory.description: Inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame as a member of Deep Purple.

name: Bebeto
milestone_by_age_26: Won the 1983 FIFA U-20 World Cup with Brazil at age 19 and became a prolific striker for Flamengo (144 goals in 286 appearances), earning his first senior Brazil cap at 21 and an Olympic silver medal at 24.
starting_point: Born in 1964 in Salvador, Brazil; began his youth career at Vitória in 1981 before moving to Flamengo in 1983.
current_position: Retired Brazilian footballer; entered politics and was elected to the Legislative Assembly of Rio de Janeiro in 2010.

trajectory.title: Professional debut for Vitória
trajectory.description: Made his senior debut for Vitória, scoring in his first appearance.

trajectory.title: Won FIFA U-20 World Cup and joined Flamengo
trajectory.description: Won the 1983 FIFA U-20 World Cup with Brazil; moved to Flamengo, where he scored 144 goals in 286 appearances.

trajectory.title: First senior Brazil cap
trajectory.description: Earned his first cap for the Brazil senior national team, though he didn't score in his initial appearances.

trajectory.title: Olympic silver medal with Brazil
trajectory.description: Won an Olympic silver medal with Brazil at the 1988 Seoul Olympics.

trajectory.title: Named South American Footballer of the Year
trajectory.description: Named South American Footballer of the Year; was top scorer at the 1989 Copa América which Brazil won.

trajectory.title: Won World Cup with Brazil
trajectory.description: Won the 1994 FIFA World Cup with Brazil, forming a formidable strike partnership with Romário.

trajectory.title: Olympic bronze with Brazil
trajectory.description: Won an Olympic bronze medal with Brazil at the 1996 Atlanta Olympics.

trajectory.title: Elected to Rio de Janeiro Legislative Assembly
trajectory.description: Entered politics and was elected to the Legislative Assembly of Rio de Janeiro representing the Democratic Labour Party.

name: Bobby Farrell
milestone_by_age_26: Was a member of Boney M. when their single 'Daddy Cool' was released on May 31, 1976 and became a European hit after a September 1976 TV appearance, when Farrell was 26 years old.
starting_point: Born in 1949 in San Nicolaas, Aruba; left home at 15 to work as a sailor; moved to Norway and then Germany, working as a DJ and dancer.
current_position: Died on December 30, 2010 at age 61 in Saint Petersburg, Russia, while on tour; found dead in his hotel room after complaining of breathing problems.

trajectory.title: Spotted by Frank Farian in Germany
trajectory.description: Was working as a DJ in Germany when producer Frank Farian spotted him for his new group Boney M.

trajectory.title: Boney M. hit with 'Daddy Cool'
trajectory.description: 'Daddy Cool' became a European hit after a September 1976 TV appearance, launching Boney M. to stardom.

trajectory.title: 'Rivers of Babylon' topped UK charts

trajectory.title: Rejoined Boney M.

trajectory.title: Boney M. reunion
trajectory.description: Reunited with the original female members for performances, continuing to tour under the Boney M. name.

trajectory.title: Died in Saint Petersburg
trajectory.description: Died on December 30, 2010, in a hotel room in Saint Petersburg, Russia, where he had been performing.

name: Marie Fredriksson
milestone_by_age_26: Released her debut solo album 'Het vind' on EMI Sweden in September 1984 at age 26, which peaked at number 20 on the Swedish album chart, preceded by the top-20 single 'Ännu doftar kärlek' in May 1984.
starting_point: Born in 1958 in Össjö, Sweden; was a member of punk group Strul in the late 1970s; grew up in Halmstad, Sweden.

trajectory.title: Founded Strul music festival
trajectory.description: Was a member of punk group Strul, which created their own music festival in 1979 in Sweden.

trajectory.title: Released debut solo album 'Het vind'
trajectory.description: Released her first solo album on EMI Sweden in September 1984, peaking at #20 on the Swedish album chart.

trajectory.title: Formed Roxette with Per Gessle
trajectory.description: Formed the pop-rock duo Roxette with Per Gessle, releasing debut album 'Pearls of Passion.'

trajectory.title: Roxette international breakthrough
trajectory.description: Released 'Look Sharp!' which produced 'The Look' and 'Listen to Your Heart,' both reaching #1 on the Billboard Hot 100.

trajectory.title: 'It Must Have Been Love' global hit
trajectory.description: 'It Must Have Been Love' was featured on the 'Pretty Woman' soundtrack, topping charts in over 10 countries.

trajectory.title: Released 'Joyride'
trajectory.description: Released the album 'Joyride,' which cemented Roxette as global superstars with over 80 million records sold.

trajectory.title: Diagnosed with brain tumor
trajectory.description: Diagnosed with a brain tumor after collapsing at home; underwent treatment that cost her vision in her right eye.

trajectory.title: Died after 17-year cancer battle
trajectory.description: Died on December 9, 2019, following a 17-year battle with cancer stemming from her brain tumor.

name: Andrew Wiles
milestone_by_age_26: Co-authored with John Coates the paper 'On the Conjecture of Birch and Swinnerton-Dyer' (Inventiones Mathematicae, 1977) at age 24, making the first progress on one of mathematics' fundamental conjectures, and became Assistant Professor at Harvard University the same year.
starting_point: Born in 1953 in Cambridge, England; father was a theology professor at Cambridge; discovered Fermat's Last Theorem at age 10 in a library book and was captivated for life.
current_position: Regius Professor of Mathematics at Oxford University; retired from Princeton in 2012; knighted in 2000; awarded the Abel Prize in 2016.

trajectory.title: Graduated from Oxford
trajectory.description: Completed his BA at Merton College, Oxford, before moving to Clare College, Cambridge for graduate studies.

trajectory.title: Co-authored Birch-Swinnerton-Dyer paper
trajectory.description: Co-authored with John Coates the first progress on the Birch-Swinnerton-Dyer conjecture; became Assistant Professor at Harvard.

trajectory.title: Completed PhD at Cambridge
trajectory.description: Awarded his PhD from Cambridge for thesis 'Reciprocity laws and the conjecture of Birch and Swinnerton-Dyer.'

trajectory.title: Professor at Princeton
trajectory.description: Appointed professor of mathematics at Princeton University.

trajectory.title: Proved main conjecture of Iwasawa theory
trajectory.description: Collaborated with Barry Mazur to prove the main conjecture of Iwasawa theory, a landmark in number theory.

trajectory.title: Proved Fermat's Last Theorem
trajectory.description: After seven years of secret work, proved Fermat's Last Theorem with Richard Taylor, solving a 350-year-old problem.

trajectory.title: Knighted by Queen Elizabeth II
trajectory.description: Made Knight Commander of the Order of the British Empire for services to mathematics.

trajectory.title: Awarded Abel Prize
trajectory.description: Received the Abel Prize, mathematics' highest honor, for his proof of Fermat's Last Theorem.

name: Gene Simmons
milestone_by_age_26: Co-founded the rock band KISS in January 1973 at age 23, releasing three studio albums by age 26 including the debut 'Kiss' (Feb 1974) and 'Dressed to Kill' (Mar 1975).

current_position: Retired from KISS after their final show in December 2023; entrepreneur and television personality; net worth estimated at $400 million.

trajectory.title: Co-founded Wicked Lester

trajectory.title: Co-founded KISS
trajectory.description: Co-founded KISS in January 1973 with Paul Stanley, Ace Frehley, and Peter Criss, adopting the 'Demon' persona.

trajectory.title: Released KISS debut album
trajectory.description: Released the self-titled debut album 'Kiss' in February 1974 on Casablanca Records.

trajectory.title: Released 'Dressed to Kill'
trajectory.description: Released 'Dressed to Kill' in March 1975, featuring the hit single 'Rock and Roll All Nite.'

trajectory.title: Released 'KISS Alive II'
trajectory.description: Released 'Alive II,' as KISS became one of America's most successful rock bands and a pop culture phenomenon.

trajectory.title: KISS unmasked era
trajectory.description: KISS removed their makeup, beginning the 'unmasked era' with the platinum album 'Lick It Up.'

trajectory.title: Original KISS reunion tour
trajectory.description: The original lineup reunited with makeup for a massively successful tour grossing $143.7 million.

trajectory.title: Inducted into Rock and Roll Hall of Fame
trajectory.description: KISS was inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame.

trajectory.title: KISS final show
trajectory.description: KISS performed their final show at Madison Square Garden in December 2023, ending a 50-year career.

name: Andrés Escobar
milestone_by_age_26: By age 22, Escobar had debuted for Atlético Nacional's senior team (1986, age 19), helped the club win the 1989 Copa Libertadores—the most prestigious club tournament in South American football—and the 1989 Copa Interamericana, and played at the 1990 FIFA World Cup for Colombia.
starting_point: Born in 1967 in Medellín, Colombia; grew up in a middle-class family; joined Atlético Nacional's youth system as a teenager.
current_position: Died on July 2, 1994 at age 27 in Medellín, Colombia; murdered shortly after the 1994 World Cup in an apparent retaliation for scoring an own goal.

trajectory.title: Debuted for Atlético Nacional
trajectory.description: Made his senior debut for Atlético Nacional, beginning a career as a central defender with the Colombian club.

trajectory.title: Colombia national team debut
trajectory.description: Earned his first cap for the Colombia national team, becoming a regular in the defense.

trajectory.title: Won Copa Libertadores with Atlético Nacional
trajectory.description: Helped Atlético Nacional win the 1989 Copa Libertadores, the first Colombian club to win South America's top club prize.

trajectory.title: Played at 1990 World Cup
trajectory.description: Represented Colombia at the 1990 FIFA World Cup in Italy, starting in the group stage matches.

trajectory.title: Scored own goal at 1994 World Cup
trajectory.description: Scored an own goal in Colombia's 2-1 loss to the United States at the 1994 World Cup on June 22.

trajectory.title: Murdered in Medellín
trajectory.description: Was shot and killed on July 2, 1994, in Medellín, reportedly in retaliation for the own goal; his death shocked the football world.

name: Anna Netrebko
milestone_by_age_26: Won the Mikhail Glinka vocal competition in 1993 at age 22 and made her operatic stage debut at the Mariinsky Theatre in 1994 at age 22 as Susanna in The Marriage of Figaro, followed by her US debut at San Francisco Opera in 1995 and entry into the Merola Opera Program in 1996.

trajectory.description: Won the prestigious Mikhail Glinka vocal competition, launching her professional career.

trajectory.title: Operatic debut at Mariinsky Theatre
trajectory.description: Made her stage debut at the Mariinsky Theatre as Susanna in 'The Marriage of Figaro.'

trajectory.title: US debut at San Francisco Opera
trajectory.description: Made her United States debut at the San Francisco Opera, entering the Merola Opera Program in 1996.

trajectory.title: Metropolitan Opera debut
trajectory.description: Made her debut at the Metropolitan Opera in New York, establishing herself on the world's biggest opera stage.

trajectory.title: Named Musician of the Year
trajectory.description: Named Musical America's Musician of the Year, cementing her status as a global opera superstar.

trajectory.title: Performed at Sochi Olympics opening
